questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to check over your shoulder if you use your mirrors.
Mirrors show you everything around your motorcycle.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Drivers will always see your turn signal and respond correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder before changing lanes to check for traffic you cannot see in your mirrors.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider reduce the risk of head and neck injuries?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet greatly reduces your chances of head or neck injury in an accident. All riders and passengers should wear a DOT-approved helmet.

questions.question: If you wait one hour after drinking one alcoholic drink before riding, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body gets rid of about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do with your feet?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
Keep them away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests to stay balanced. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's brake light compare to a car's brake light?

options.text: It is more noticeable than a car's brake lights.
It is less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
It is less important than a car's brake lights.
It is more easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flash your brake light before slowing or stopping to help other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: What is the proper body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean far over the bike so your arms hold you up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms bend slightly at the grips. This lets you easily reach and control all the motorcycle's controls.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see and be seen better.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see and be seen better.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and helps them see you. It keeps you away from wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Keep a longer distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn the passenger about hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger's weight. Keep more space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding your motorcycle, what is true?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Alcohol will not affect your riding skills.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine if you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body gets rid of about one drink's worth of alcohol per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which surface provides good traction for motorcycles?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, and painted lane markings all have poor traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface for motorcycles.

questions.question: Studies show that motorcycles with headlights on during the day are:

options.text: Not as easy to see as other vehicles.
More visible to other drivers than when headlights are off.
Less safe than when headlights are off.

questions.correctAnswerText: More visible to other drivers than when headlights are off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on when you ride, day or night. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates all have poor traction. Dry pavement is the safest surface for a motorcycle.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see far to the sides when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see far to the sides when riding.
questions.explanation: An approved helmet allows you to see clearly to the sides for safe riding. Approved helmets have labels with the maker's name, instructions, and safety standard information.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes and helps prevent problems before you ride.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly reduces the chance of serious head or neck injury in a crash. It will not limit your vision or make riding harder.

questions.question: Which fabric offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Add extra lights to your motorcycle. Wear bright or reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and flash your brake light to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, you should:
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoe laces securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle while riding.

questions.question: When checking your tires before a ride, you do NOT need to check:
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread depth, and general wear.

questions.question: As a motorcycle rider, how can you help others see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to be more visible. Also use your headlight at all times and use your turn signals.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no visible defects like cracks or loose padding.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. DOT and state standards, fits snugly around your head, and has no visible defects like cracks or loose padding. How it looks is not important for protection.

questions.question: A street-legal motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Street-legal motorcycles must have brakes, headlight, taillight, stop lamp, muffler, horn, rearview mirror, and a seat. A windshield wiper is not required.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding a motorcycle.
